page: Amazon Web Services c6g.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance powered by custom AWS Graviton2 processors utilizing the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the server provisions 4 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core running at 2.5 GHz, avoiding hyperthreading resource contention. The processor configuration includes 64 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, 32 MB L3 cache, and integrated AES hardware cryptography acceleration, paired with 8.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per core) reflecting a standard 1:2 compute-optimized ratio.

Storage and network configurations are lean, as the c6g.xlarge provides no local NVMe storage and relies entirely on remote EBS volumes. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 1 Gbps, and no discrete GPUs are present. Benchmark results show average single-core stress-ng throughput (1519.79) alongside average uncached memory transfer rates of 71.99 GB/sec read and 35.14 GB/sec write. However, multi-core stress-ng (6053.66), Geekbench scores (965 single-core, 3252 multi-core), and overall PassMark metrics position the system in the lower performance quartiles relative to high-end x86 counterparts.

From an efficiency standpoint, the c6g.xlarge offers predictable CPU core utilization and power efficiency native to the Graviton2 platform. Workload throughput metrics include 4.76 million Redis SET operations per second and 4.95 GB/sec static web serving throughput. These characteristics make the instance suitable for arm64-compatible services, containerized web hosting, CI/CD compile runners, batch processing, and lightweight application tiers that do not demand extensive local I/O or specialized x86 vector extensions.
description: Amazon Web Services c6g.xlarge is an arm64 compute-optimized instance powered by AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 processors running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It delivers 4 dedicated physical cores at a 2.5 GHz clock speed with a single thread per core, backed by 8.0 GB of system memory at 2.0 GB per core. The server includes no bundled local storage and features a 1 Gbps baseline network throughput without GPU acceleration. In benchmark evaluations, the c6g.xlarge provides average single-core stress-ng performance and solid uncached memory throughput, balanced against lower relative multi-core and PassMark composite scores. Offering predictable dedicated compute execution for ARM environments, the instance is well suited for containerized microservices, build pipelines, web serving, and general batch compute workloads.
